column3: Its dispersed dust gives the closest physical analogue for the focus's transformation of deeds into scattered particles.
The magicians' profession of faith does not clarify the judgment on deeds in the focus.
Its fixed divine term supplies only a distant frame for the judgment that reaches human deeds.
It shows evil deeds becoming manifest and their mockery enclosing their doers, closely framing the focus's adverse reckoning.
The local denial of resurrection after witnessing punishment helps situate the focus's coming judgment within the surah.
It explicitly joins disbelief to works becoming weightless at the Resurrection, directly clarifying the focus's loss of lasting value.
It repeats the same appearance of evil deeds and ensuing consequence already supplied by 45:33.
Its warning mission belongs to the surah but adds little about deeds being turned to dust.
The promise for believing righteous deeds provides a limited contrast to the focus's failed deeds.
Its scattered pearls use similar dispersion imagery, but in an honored rather than judgmental setting.
The completion of the magicians' confession has no clear bearing on the focus's treatment of deeds.
The scattering of stars offers a cosmic parallel for loss of ordered cohesion, though it concerns no human works.
The secure placement of the embryo does not illuminate the focus's dispersal of deeds.
The local destruction of deniers provides a punishment context for the focus's later accounting of deeds.
It connects what hands sent ahead with divine recompense, supplying an accountability frame for the focus.
Its contrast between disbelief borne by its doer and righteous deeds preparing a future place clarifies consequential action.
The promised gardens and palaces do not add to the focus's judgment on deeds.
Sending something ahead for oneself gives a limited contrast to the focus's deeds that yield no enduring result.
Human creation and testing do not specifically explain the fate of deeds in the focus.
The division of the Quran into portions supplies a structural analogue for fragmentation, reinforced by its adjacent inquiry about deeds.
It portrays choices sent ahead as provoking wrath, but adds little beyond the general accountability already established.
Its return of good or evil action upon oneself directly supports the focus's personal accounting of deeds.
The local account of Noah's people and prepared punishment reinforces the surah's pattern of judgment after rejection.
Its annulled works of unbelievers are relevant, but the verse adds no mechanism comparable to the focus's scattered dust.
Reward for the best deeds only contrasts with the focus's invalidated deeds.
The local account of idolaters' ruin contributes a surrounding judgment setting but not the treatment of deeds themselves.
It identifies associating partners with God as a cause for works being nullified, directly supplying one route to the focus's outcome.
The reporting and punishment of disbelief according to deeds gives only a broad accountability parallel.
Universal questioning about what people did adds the procedural account that precedes a judgment such as the focus's.
Divine awareness of tested conduct is only indirectly related to the focus's final evaluation of deeds.
It grounds recompense in the deeds people bring, supporting the focus's treatment of works at judgment.
The list of destroyed peoples continues the local punishment theme but is redundant with the preceding surah examples.
Noah's refusal to judge hidden deeds only loosely contrasts with the divine judgment in the focus.
The reward for righteous deeds is a broad positive contrast to works that lose all value.
Its denial of resurrection by false gods contributes a local contrast, without explaining the focus's action on deeds.
Divine sight of all deeds establishes general oversight but adds no distinct account of their fate.
God's refusal to set right the work of corrupters directly parallels deeds being rendered incapable of enduring value.
The destruction of earlier unjust generations adds a historical judgment context for the focus's reckoning of works.
The reward of workers does not materially clarify the focus's nullification of deeds.
The promise of affection for believers who do good is too remote from the focus's judgment scene.
This local summary of destroyed peoples completes the punishment sequence surrounding the focus's surah context.
God's preservation of the reward for good work sharply contrasts with the focus's deeds that become dispersed dust.
Forgetting what one's hands sent ahead and turning from signs links rejected guidance to the later reckoning of deeds.
The alternation of night, sleep, and daytime revival does not clarify the focus's judgment on works.
Its category of the greatest losers in deeds directly frames how apparently productive action can fail in the final assessment.
Calling Noah's son an unrighteous deed supplies a limited criterion of corrupt action, though not the focus's dispersal image.
Successors being observed for how they act offers only a preliminary testing frame before final judgment.
It explicitly ties both evil and good conduct to recompense, supporting the focus's moral accounting of action.
The condemned request to confront their misleaders does not clarify the focus's treatment of deeds.
Repentance joined to righteous action offers a local alternative to failed deeds but no direct explanation of their nullification.
The fixed term of communities does not add to the focus's evaluation of works.
The delayed but fixed term of punishment is not a distinct guide to deeds becoming dispersed.
Examining what one has sent ahead for tomorrow gives a general anticipatory frame, already covered by earlier accountability cards.
The command to do righteousness and God's knowledge of conduct does not explain the focus's final judgment on deeds.
A secure prior standing with God offers only a distant positive contrast to deeds that fail at judgment.
Moses receiving the Book with Aaron does not bear on the focus's evaluation of deeds.
Earthly adornment as a test of best deeds clarifies that works are evaluated by quality rather than mere appearance.
Mention of forefathers has no clear relation to the focus's judgment on deeds.
The opening declaration of a clear Book does not illuminate the focus's treatment of human works.
The mismatch between spoken excuse and hidden conduct supports accountability, but not the focus's distinctive outcome for deeds.
Degrees corresponding to deeds show a differentiated divine evaluation, complementing the focus's severe negative result.
The Creator's sovereignty and command to ask the informed do not clarify the fate of deeds.
Its fulfillment of each person's deeds without injustice reinforces that the focus's judgment is measured rather than arbitrary.
It explicitly declares both an idolatrous setting and what its people do to be vain, closely paralleling the focus's loss of value.
The local worship of what cannot benefit or harm gives background for failed devotion but no account of deeds becoming dust.
Erasing worst deeds and rewarding best ones provides a contrasting merciful treatment of deeds, not the focus's outcome.
The idolaters' admission that their gods cannot speak does not clarify the judgment on deeds.
The earthquake begins the physical sequence that ends in scattered dust, but the final image is already supplied more directly.
Recompense for deeds is a general principle already represented by more specific accountability passages.
The command for each side to act until the result is known gives only a broad test-and-outcome frame.
The local gathering and questioning of idolaters supplies a judgment setting, without addressing the fate of their deeds.
The direct warning not to invalidate one's deeds closely relates to the focus's presentation of works losing their effect.
Disavowing others' deeds distinguishes responsibility, but does not explain how deeds are assessed in the focus.
Pharaoh's threat of imprisonment has no clear relation to the focus's treatment of works.
The prohibition on acting ahead of God and the Messenger does not illuminate deeds becoming scattered dust.
God's ability to show the promised punishment adds no distinct connection to the focus's deeds.
The accusation that revelation is ancient tales does not clarify the focus's judgment on actions.
God's knowledge of the community's deeds restates general oversight without adding the focus's outcome.
The making of virgins has no bearing on the focus's evaluation of deeds.
The magicians falling in prostration does not clarify the focus's judgment on works.
The final return and report of deeds give a general accountability frame, but little beyond earlier cards.
Their embellished evil conduct and refusal to humble themselves gives a limited causal background for punitive judgment.
The descent upon those who divided revelation does not itself explain the focus's treatment of deeds.
The protective damage to a ship concerns preservation of livelihood, not the final value of deeds.
Recording what people sent ahead together with their traces explains how deeds remain available for the focus's later assessment.
Pulverized mountains continue the dust sequence, but it is redundant after the direct scattered-dust parallel.
High ranks for faithful righteous workers provide only a positive contrast to the focus's failed deeds.
The late wish to return and do otherwise shows the irreversible consequence of arriving at judgment with failed deeds.
The oath to question everyone reinforces accountability but repeats the inquiry already supplied by its adjacent passage.
The home of peace according to deeds is a broad positive contrast to the focus's adverse judgment.
Adorned deeds leading earlier peoples from the path give a limited background for why works may fail.
Repentance after wrongdoing gives an alternative to unresolved evil deeds, rather than clarifying the focus's outcome.
The promised elevation of the oppressed does not bear on the focus's judgment on works.
The excellence of calling to God while doing good does not add to the focus's account of nullified deeds.
The distinction between clear and ambiguous verses is not a meaningful guide to the focus's treatment of deeds.
The final regret at not having sent something ahead for life sharply underscores the focus's irreversible judgment horizon.
Ships moving on the sea do not clarify the focus's treatment of human deeds.
The mutual separation of responsibility for deeds supports personal accountability but adds little about their final fate.
The command to show humility to believing followers does not bear on the focus's judgment on deeds.
Sending good ahead and finding it with God provides a direct positive contrast to the focus's deeds that cannot endure.
It gives the nearest parallel: disbelievers' deeds are ashes scattered by wind, making their inability to retain any gain explicit.
It directly states that apostasy makes deeds come to nothing in this world and the Hereafter.
It explicitly describes deeds becoming void in both worlds and their doers losing all support.
It identifies disbelief in faith as rendering one's work futile, supplying a direct cause of the focus's outcome.
It states that association with God would nullify even the deeds of the prophets, sharply clarifying the vulnerability of works.
It declares the deeds of those who deny the signs and final meeting to be worthless, then ties recompense to what they did.
It explicitly says the works of those who maintain worship alongside disbelief are nullified.
It says that prior peoples' works became worthless in this world and the Hereafter, joining failed action to loss.
It portrays worldly-directed action as leaving nothing in the Hereafter and declares what was made there void.
Its contrast between what perishes and what remains with God helps explain why some work cannot endure.
It shows the worldly seeker receiving a limited immediate portion before facing blameworthy rejection in the Hereafter.
It contrasts the focus by affirming that a believer's striving for the Hereafter is received and appreciated.
It names those whose effort is lost in worldly life while they mistakenly think they are doing well.
It completes the nearby account of failed deeds by naming Hell as the recompense for disbelief and mockery.
The just scales of the Resurrection supply the evaluative setting in which the focus's deeds are found without weight.
It makes the heaviness of a person's scales the mark of success, directly contrasting with deeds reduced to dust.
It identifies light scales as loss, closely complementing the focus's image of works with no retained substance.
The local scene of angels giving criminals no good news immediately establishes the punitive day in which the focus occurs.
Its contrasting outcome for the companions of Paradise completes the local division that follows the focus's failed deeds.
It gives the decisive opposite transformation: God changes repented evil deeds into good deeds rather than scattering them.
It compares disbelievers' deeds to a mirage that vanishes on arrival, directly paralleling the focus's dissolution of apparent work.
It contrasts empty speech with righteous action that is raised, clarifying that enduring value depends on the kind of work.
It explicitly says that those who disbelieve and bar God's path have their deeds made vain.
It directly joins hatred of revelation to God making deeds vain.
It identifies following what angers God and disliking His pleasure as the cause for works being made void.
Its assurance that God will not let believers' deeds go to waste provides a precise positive contrast to the focus.
It limits each person to what they strove for, grounding the focus's treatment of deeds in personal responsibility.
It states that striving will be seen, supplying the disclosure stage before the focus's judgment of works.
It completes that sequence with full recompense, clarifying the result of disclosed effort.
It describes God removing evil deeds at the final gathering, an opposite divine treatment that highlights the focus's severity.
It pairs reverence with God erasing evil deeds and magnifying reward, directly contrasting retained and removed action.
It asks believers for repentance that causes God to erase evil deeds, providing a remedial contrast to the focus.
Receiving one's record in the right hand supplies the successful counterpart to the focus's adverse accounting of deeds.
It states that on the great event a person remembers what they strove for, supplying the recollective judgment horizon.
It says every soul will know what it sent ahead and left behind, closely framing the final review of deeds.
It affirms that even an atom's weight of good is seen, intensifying the contrast with works dispersed beyond weight.
It extends that exact accounting to the least evil, supporting the focus's comprehensive judgment of action.
It makes heavy scales the condition of success, a direct contrast to the focus's scattering of deeds.
It makes light scales the condition of ruin, closely clarifying the consequence of works that retain no weight.
God's assurance that He does not let any worker's deed be lost gives an exact positive contrast to the focus's dispersed deeds.
It describes deeds becoming worthless after a false profession of faith is exposed, directly reinforcing the possibility of annulled work.
It assures the faithful worker of no injustice or deprivation, contrasting the focus's adverse assessment with equitable preservation.
It explicitly describes God removing believers' evil deeds and rewarding their best deeds, an opposite treatment of moral action.
The local confirmation that the worshippers have denied and cannot avert punishment directly leads into the focus's judgment scene.
The deniers' refusal to expect the final meeting introduces the local unbelief that the following judgment exposes.
The sky's splitting and descent of angels supplies the Day-of-Judgment setting that contains the focus's assessment of deeds.
The true dominion and grievous day for disbelievers continue the immediate scene of judgment around the focus.
Gathering people on their faces toward Hell gives a later surah instance of the same adverse final destination.
